# installation/windows

Canonical: https://paneflow.dev/docs/installation/windows

<!-- Public mirror of paneflow.dev. Regenerated by scripts/sync-public-docs.ts
     in the site repo. If this checked-in copy is hotfixed, backport the same
     change to the site source before the next sync. -->

Paneflow ships a **native Windows build** since v0.5.0. The supported
path on Windows is the `.msi` installer for **Windows 10 (1809+) and
Windows 11** (x86\_64). Running the Linux build under WSL2 + WSLg still
works as an alternative if you already live inside WSL2.

  **TL;DR.** Download `paneflow-<version>-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.msi`
  from the [download page](/download) or the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases),
  run it, and launch Paneflow from the Start menu. New terminals default
  to PowerShell.

## Frequently asked questions about Paneflow on Windows [#frequently-asked-questions-about-paneflow-on-windows]

### How do I install Paneflow on Windows? [#how-do-i-install-paneflow-on-windows]

1. Open the [download page](/download) and pick the Windows build, or
   grab the `.msi` directly from the
   [latest release](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/latest):

   ```text
   paneflow-<version>-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.msi
   ```

2. Run the installer and follow the prompts. Paneflow installs as a
   standard Windows app.

3. Launch Paneflow from the Start menu. New terminals open PowerShell by
   default; you can change the shell in Settings.

x86\_64 is the published Windows target. An ARM64 Windows installer is
not built yet.

### Does Paneflow run on Windows 10 or only Windows 11? [#does-paneflow-run-on-windows-10-or-only-windows-11]

Both. The native build targets Windows 10 version 1809 and later, and
Windows 11. The title bar renders native Windows 11 caption buttons on
11; on 10 it uses the standard window controls.

### Can I still run Paneflow under WSL2? [#can-i-still-run-paneflow-under-wsl2]

Yes. WSL2 + WSLg remains a fully supported alternative, which is handy
if your toolchains, paths, and `apt`-installed agents already live
inside WSL2. The Linux build runs there unchanged.

1. **Enable WSL2** (if not already installed). Open PowerShell as
   Administrator:

   ```powershell
   wsl --install
   ```

   This installs WSL2 with the default Ubuntu distribution. Reboot when
   prompted.

2. **Update WSLg** (ships by default on Windows 11; on Windows 10 you
   install it manually, see the
   [Microsoft WSLg docs](https://github.com/microsoft/wslg)).

3. **Install Paneflow's Linux `.deb`** inside the WSL2 distribution:

   ```bash
   VERSION=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/arthjean/paneflow/releases/latest \
     | grep -oE '"tag_name":\s*"v[^"]+"' | cut -d\" -f4 | sed 's/^v//')
   ARCH=$(uname -m)
   curl -fLO "https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/download/v${VERSION}/paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.deb"
   sudo apt install "./paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.deb"
   paneflow
   ```

   The Paneflow window opens as a native Windows window via WSLg's
   Wayland forwarding.

### Should I use the native build or WSL2? [#should-i-use-the-native-build-or-wsl2]

Use the native `.msi` for tighter Windows integration: Windows
notifications, the Windows file picker, and a native title bar. Stick
with WSL2 if you already do most of your work inside a WSL2 Linux
environment and want Paneflow to share that filesystem and toolchain.

### Does Paneflow work with Windows Terminal? [#does-paneflow-work-with-windows-terminal]

Paneflow is itself a terminal workspace, so you run it *instead of*
Windows Terminal, not inside it. Windows Terminal hosts traditional
command-line shells (PowerShell, `cmd.exe`, WSL bash); Paneflow is a
graphical multi-pane workspace built for orchestrating CLI coding
agents, and runs as a standard Windows app.

### How do I update Paneflow on Windows? [#how-do-i-update-paneflow-on-windows]

Re-run the latest `.msi`, which upgrades the existing install in place.
The in-app updater also detects new releases and points you to the
matching Windows build.
